correctness.rationale: For \(b>0\) and \(C^3\) even, half-wave antisymmetric forcing strictly decreasing on its first half, weighted integration constructs an exactly periodic orbit with two simple crossings. Time-map convexity and parameter monotonicity establish the global 0/1/2 count; reversible dynamics pairs the two solutions. Differentiation of crossing times gives \(P_{uu}=2bQ>0\) and \(P_c=-2(1-e^{-bL})/b<0\), proving the explicit square-root branch opening and multiplier formulas. Standard-library numerical checks of a two-harmonic example are supplemental, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Full original Gasull–Zhao 2023 text gives an upper bound of two periodic solutions and a qualitative rotated-vector-field fold, not an evaluated bias threshold for the infinite-dimensional even antiperiodic forcing class or its exact local square-root coefficient. The full 2024 trig-coefficient paper proves finiteness and upper bounds, with implicit half maps; it does not imply the explicit general half-wave weighted functional. An older 2004 constant-slope cosine subfamily is a serious priority risk for the one-frequency specialization, but that stated forcing class does not dominate arbitrary monotone half-wave inputs. Indexed mathematical literature records returned no equivalent claim; this alone is not novelty proof.
residual_risks: Older 2004 cosine-specialized paper could evaluate the single-frequency critical threshold; its full text was not accessible following bounded lawful access attempts.
The 2007 general piecewise paper and unindexed works could use equivalent reversible forcing functionals; their full texts were not inspected.
Mathematical-index and literature retrieval do not establish exhaustive publication priority.

value.rationale: The forcing threshold is an exact natural bifurcation invariant for every strictly decreasing symmetric half-wave input, rather than an isolated model parameter. It supplies the complete entrainment count, sharp local branch separation and transverse stability; two-frequency forcing shows a nontrivial, computable response to waveform shape. The qualitative two-cycle bound alone does not determine these quantities, making the full infinite-dimensional statement mathematically motivated and useful.
